pipeline.title: YouTube Data API
pipeline.detail: 16 Albanian, Serbian and English queries · search.list, commentThreads.list, channels.list · 3445 quota units

pipeline.title: Pseudonymise
pipeline.detail: HMAC-SHA256 with a server secret. Channel IDs and names are dropped before storage.

pipeline.title: SQLite store
pipeline.detail: Scoped comment IDs; re-fetching a video adds nothing twice.

pipeline.title: Coordination engine
pipeline.detail: Timing bursts, language (Geg/standard doublets, calques), shared talking points, network signals.

pipeline.title: Bot model
pipeline.detail: LightGBM + relational GNN, calibrated. Learned weights, no hand-set rules.

pipeline.title: Analyst
pipeline.detail: 2 videos at Level 1, 30 at Level 2, 15 at Level 3, 22 quiet. A human decides.

weights.name: Near-duplicate posts shared with other accounts
Share of posts that are replies
Spread of activity over the day
Size of the largest copy-paste group joined (log)
Accounts it posts in sync with (log)
Accounts active with it in the same minutes (log)

bench: F1 on bot types never seen in training
tested: Account-profile model: external sets never used in training
model.transfer: Transfer check: applied to these 7,188 YouTube accounts, the Twitter-trained model flags 100% of them as bots. Most YouTube commenters post once and have no follower data, which the Twitter model never saw. So this page does not label anyone a bot: accounts are ranked by the coordination engine, and a Kosovo-labelled sample is the next step.
